Title: 3 Habits Making Your Melasma Worse (Not Just Sun)

Description:
Melasma affects an estimated 5 to 6 million women in the US, and more than 80% of people with melasma have a history of using oral contraceptives. UV exposure and hormones start it, but two everyday habits keep it going: applying sunscreen just once a day, and picking or scrubbing irritated skin.

Watch to find out why 66.8% of people with melasma develop dark marks after acne, and the simple fixes - from tinted sunscreen to the foods that help skin repair itself.

platforms.caption:
Your melasma keeps getting darker - and it's not just the sun ☀️

Reapplying sunscreen just once a day and picking at irritated skin both quietly make melasma worse. 66.8% of people with melasma develop dark marks after acne, compared to 24.1% of people without it.

Reapply SPF 30+ every 2 hours (tinted with iron oxide blocks visible light too), keep your hands off breakouts, and add vitamin C-rich foods like citrus and salmon.
